claims.text: Calling toString on an Output<T> in Pulumi produces placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in logs, generated files, or resource properties.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ titled 'Output value errors' covering this and other symptoms of treating an output as a plain value.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering output value errors.
In Pulumi, errors arise from stringifying, branching on, or reading an output value like a plain value.
Pulumi returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when an update conflicts.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
On Apple Silicon Macs, x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs.
The Pulumi CLI produces `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it cannot access a self-managed state backend.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
`pulumi` supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds providing bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.

Converting a Pulumi output value to a string directly (without apply or an equivalent helper) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.
In Pulumi TypeScript, string conversion of an Output yields text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Pulumi Python, converting an Output to string yields text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` should be used instead.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In Pulumi C#, string conversion of an Output yields text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to string throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.

String-composition helpers for outputs: `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript; `Output.concat`, `Output.format`, `Output.json_dumps` in Python; `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go; `Output.Format` in C#.
An `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so an outer variable assigned inside it is undefined when read earlier.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, but a few positions such as a resource's logical name cannot.

In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on a Pulumi output is generally always true because the Output object itself is evaluated; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error since Output<bool> is not a bool.
Values known when the program starts, such as stack config read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an output as a resource logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, `range(some_output)` with a Pulumi Output raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the output object itself.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously read a resolved value out of an output.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).

Cross-referenced pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs.
